(10.) Other Utilities
The remaining utilities provided through sources other than the City include electric power, gas and telephone service.
a. Electrical Service
Electrical Service to the City, SMSA and the project is supplied by the Pennsylvania Power and Light (PP&L). Harrisburg's electrical power could come from one of nine PP&L Power Plants, the largest one being the Keystone Plant stationed in the Western Pennsylvania soft coal fields near Indiana, Pennsylvania. Approximately 97 percent of PP&L's electricity is produced from coal... 4 percent from hydro power and 3 percent from diesel oil power generation units.
Other than the private customers served by the Company, PP&L also provides service to the City Government in the forms of electrical power and contract service of street lighting, installation, and maintenance.
The Street lights provided by the company are of two principal types-incandescent and mercury vapor. Street lighting in the Project appears to be adequate along the arterial areas. Front Street and Second Street are both lit with the mercury vapor lamps of 20,000 lumens each. Some of the major streets intersecting Second and Front Streets are also lit in this fashion (Broad, Ruley, Maclay Streets). For the best part, the interior residential portions of the project area have incandescent lighting. These vary in output from 6,000 to 2,500 lumens. In some areas tree foliage, during the summer months, tends to block the lighting capacity of weaker incandescent street lights.
Power Company Officials indicate that additional power requirements for the project area could be met; however, in some cases the developer may experience some additional out of pocket expense in obtaining service.
b. Gas Service
Natural gas is supplied to the Harrisburg area by the UGI Corporation. Gas service is available to all properties in the project area and gas mains are in all of the major streets. UGI indicates that approximately 50 percent of the properties in the project area have and use their service. Many of the property owners continue to heat with fuel oil and a few have converted to electric heat.
The Company also indicates that, despite the fact that there is a high-pressure gas main in the project area, running along Front Street, they may not be able to supply a new development classed as investment (medium or high-rise apartments are included in their classification) due to the national shortages of natural gas supplies and their previous commitments to existing customers.
